title: Cloud Resource Allocation
short_description: Provision minimum cluster node RAM capacities using binary search on answer, maximize single-server VM billing revenue, pack servers using First-Fit Decreasing, and sort container workloads.
real_world_context: Hyperscale cloud providers (such as AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure) and container orchestration platforms (such as Kubernetes) continuously bin-pack virtual machines (VMs) and containerized microservices onto bare-metal server infrastructure. Cluster autoscalers use Binary Search on Answer to determine the minimum per-node RAM capacity needed to schedule sequential pod deployment manifests across at most K nodes, cloud billing optimizers solve 0/1 Knapsack models to maximize monthly VM rental revenues on high-performance host servers, datacenter schedulers apply the First-Fit Decreasing (FFD) greedy bin packing heuristic to minimize the number of booted physical machines, and container orchestrators sort multi-dimensional compute demands to prioritize heavy workloads.
learning_objectives: Apply Binary Search on Answer over monotonic capacity spaces to determine minimum server node provisioning thresholds.
Solve 0/1 Knapsack dynamic programming to maximize server VM rental revenue under physical memory constraints.
Implement the First-Fit Decreasing (FFD) greedy heuristic to bin-pack batch workloads into the minimum number of physical servers.
Sort containerized workloads by multi-resource computational demands (CPU cores and RAM).
Use Max Flow algorithms to optimize the placement of containers across multiple servers with capacity constraints.
